name: org.machanism.machai:mcp-server-maven-plugin
description: The MCP Server Maven Plugin integrates a Machai Model Context Protocol (MCP) server into Maven builds. It provides aggregator goals for stateless and streamable HTTP transports, starts one server for a Maven project or multi-module reactor, and supplies the current project name, version, and base directory to that server. Configuration is loaded through a PropertiesConfigurator, while values supplied through params become JVM system properties only when an equivalent property is not already set. The plugin registers configured Machai AI tools and exposes them to MCP-compatible HTTP clients without requiring a separate launcher. It is intended for local development, integration testing, demonstrations, and build-driven AI automation. A lifecycle function tool permits an MCP client to request a delayed, orderly JVM shutdown with a selected exit code.

usageContext: Invoke an MCP server directly from a Maven build
Expose configured Machai AI tools to MCP HTTP clients
Run one aggregator server for a multi-module Maven reactor
Choose stateless or streamable HTTP MCP transport
Support local development, demonstrations, and repeatable integration tests

constructors.description: Creates the Maven Mojo behind the stateless aggregator goal. Maven normally constructs and injects this component; users invoke it through the fully qualified plugin goal rather than instantiating it directly.

examples.description: Direct construction is primarily useful in tests. In normal use Maven creates the Mojo and injects its project, base directory, port, configuration file, and parameter map.

constructors.description: Creates the Maven Mojo behind the streamable HTTP aggregator goal. Maven normally owns construction and configuration of this component.

examples.description: Direct construction can support unit tests; production usage should invoke the streamable Maven goal so Maven supplies all required context.

features.name: stateless
features.description: Starts a stateless HTTP MCP server as an aggregator goal. It applies parameters, loads the configured server settings, uses Maven project metadata and the base directory, sets the required port, registers tools, and reports startup or configuration failures as Maven execution errors.

examples.description: Runs a stateless MCP endpoint on port 8080 using the specified readable configuration file. Invoke it from the Maven project or reactor root that the server should represent.

features.name: streamable
features.description: Starts a streamable HTTP MCP server as an aggregator goal. It follows the same project-aware configuration flow as the stateless goal while selecting the streamable MCP transport expected by compatible clients.

examples.description: Runs the streamable HTTP transport on port 8080 after loading the supplied Machai MCP properties configuration.

features.name: stop-mcp-server
features.description: Allows an MCP client to request server termination. The operation immediately acknowledges the request, starts delayed shutdown processing, records final usage statistics, and exits the JVM with the requested code; the exit code defaults to zero when omitted by the function caller.

examples.description: Illustrates the underlying Java call with a successful process exit code. In normal operation an MCP client invokes the exposed stop-mcp-server function after completing its work.

customizations.name: mcp.port
customizations.description: Required Maven property selecting the HTTP listening port for either server goal.

examples.description: Selects TCP port 8080 when invoking a goal from the command line.

customizations.name: mcp.config
customizations.description: Path to a readable configuration file accepted by the Machai PropertiesConfigurator and used for server and tool settings.

examples.description: Supplies the configuration file when starting either HTTP transport.

customizations.name: params
customizations.description: Map of additional key/value settings copied to JVM system properties only if a property with the same name is not already set, preserving explicit runtime overrides.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.mcp.maven.AbstractMCPServerMojo
studs.description: Common Maven boundary for MCP server transports. It centralizes injected project configuration, parameter application, credential handling, and PropertiesConfigurator loading for concrete transport goals.

examples.name: Install, configure, and run the stateless server
examples.description: A complete Maven-plugin workflow for a stateless MCP endpoint.
steps: Install Java 17 or newer and Apache Maven 3.8.1 or newer.
Make the released plugin available from Maven Central, or build this source checkout and run mvn install for the 1.4.1-SNAPSHOT version.
Create a readable /path/to/mcp.properties file containing the Machai server, tool, and provider settings required by your environment.
From the target Maven project or multi-module reactor root, run mvn org.machanism.machai:mcp-server-maven-plugin:1.4.1-SNAPSHOT:stateless -Dmcp.port=8080 -Dmcp.config=/path/to/mcp.properties.
Connect an MCP-compatible HTTP client to the server endpoint on port 8080 and invoke the configured tools.
When work is complete, invoke the exposed stop-mcp-server function with exit-code 0 for an orderly delayed shutdown.

examples.name: Configure the plugin in a POM and run streamable HTTP
examples.description: Pins the plugin version and supplies shared configuration in pom.xml before invoking its streamable goal.
steps: Add org.machanism.machai:mcp-server-maven-plugin:1.4.1-SNAPSHOT under build plugins in pom.xml.
Inside the plugin configuration set port to 8080 and configFile to /path/to/mcp.properties.
Run mvn org.machanism.machai:mcp-server-maven-plugin:1.4.1-SNAPSHOT:streamable from the reactor root.
Connect a client that supports streamable HTTP MCP and use the configured tools.
